storyOverview.userStory: As a system, I want agentic orchestration framework integrated per Story 3.0.8 decisions, so that multi-step analytical workflows can be planned and executed using AWS Strands.
storyOverview.technicalSummary:
Story 3.1 implements the AWS Strands agentic framework foundation for Epic 3, establishing the orchestration layer that will coordinate Retrieval, Analysis, and Synthesis agents in Stories 3.2-3.4. This story focuses on framework setup, basic 2-step workflow validation, and state management infrastructure.
Key Implementation: Initialize AWS Strands orchestrator with MistralModel, implement basic @tool decorator pattern, validate 2-step workflow execution (Retrieve → Synthesize).

scopeBoundaries.inScope: - AWS Strands v1.15.0 initialization with MistralModel - Basic orchestrator setup in raglite/orchestration/orchestrator.py - 2-step workflow validation (minimal agents for testing) - State management infrastructure (AgentTask, AgentResult models) - Error handling foundation (timeout, failure detection) - Integration test proving framework execution - Developer documentation for @tool pattern usage
scopeBoundaries.outOfScope: - Complete agent implementations (Stories 3.2-3.4) - Multi-step complex workflows (Story 3.5) - MCP tool integration (Story 3.6) - Production-level error handling (Story 3.7) - Comprehensive test suite (Story 3.8)

decision.title: AWS Strands Framework Confirmed
decision.rationale: Story 3.0.8 evaluated 3 frameworks and selected AWS Strands (84.5% weighted score). No changes to framework selection - Story 3.1 implements the approved decision.
decision.impact: - Use strands.Agent, strands.tool imports throughout orchestration module - MistralModel integration (no AWS Bedrock dependencies) - @tool decorator pattern for all agent definitions

decision.title: Orchestration Module Structure
decision.rationale: Follow Sequential Chain pattern (Pattern 1) from epic-3-agent-patterns.md. Simple linear workflow for initial implementation, parallelism deferred to Story 3.5.
decision.impact: - orchestrator.py: Main Agent initialization and workflow execution - models.py: Pydantic models for AgentTask, AgentResult, WorkflowPlan - fallback.py: Error handling foundation (expanded in Story 3.7) - *_agent.py files: Individual agent implementations (Stories 3.2-3.4)

decision.title: Model Selection for Orchestration
decision.rationale: Use Mistral Small (mistral-small-latest) for orchestrator decisions. Tunable to Claude Sonnet in future if performance issues arise. Ricardo confirmed Mistral works without AWS Bedrock in Story 3.0.8.
decision.impact: - MistralModel(api_key=settings.mistral_api_key, model_id="mistral-small-latest") - Expected orchestration overhead: 3-5 seconds per workflow - Cost-effective compared to Claude Sonnet ($0.25/MTok vs $3/MTok)

module.name: raglite/orchestration/models.py
module.purpose: Pydantic models for workflow state management
module.keyPatterns: - AgentTask: task_id, agent_type, instruction, depends_on - AgentResult: task_id, agent_type, success, result, execution_time_ms, error - WorkflowPlan: query, complexity, tasks, estimated_duration_ms - QueryComplexity enum: SIMPLE, ANALYTICAL - AgentType enum: RETRIEVAL, ANALYSIS, SYNTHESIS
module.codeSnippet:
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field from typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional from enum import Enum
class QueryComplexity(str, Enum): SIMPLE = "simple" ANALYTICAL = "analytical"
class AgentType(str, Enum): RETRIEVAL = "retrieval" ANALYSIS = "analysis" SYNTHESIS = "synthesis"
class AgentTask(BaseModel): task_id: str agent_type: AgentType instruction: str depends_on: Optional[List[str]] = None
class AgentResult(BaseModel): task_id: str agent_type: AgentType success: bool result: Any execution_time_ms: int error: Optional[str] = None
class WorkflowPlan(BaseModel): query: str complexity: QueryComplexity tasks: List[AgentTask] estimated_duration_ms: int
module.testingNotes: - Unit test: Pydantic model validation (required fields, types) - Unit test: Serialization/deserialization (model_dump(), model_validate())

module.name: raglite/orchestration/fallback.py
module.purpose: Basic error handling and graceful degradation foundation
module.keyPatterns: - Timeout detection and handling - Exception catching and logging - Partial result extraction - Basic fallback to Epic 2 retrieval (full implementation in Story 3.7)
module.codeSnippet:
import logging from typing import Optional from raglite.orchestration.models import AgentResult
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
class WorkflowTimeoutError(Exception): """Raised when workflow exceeds timeout threshold.""" pass
class AgentExecutionError(Exception): """Raised when agent fails during execution.""" pass
async def handle_workflow_failure( error: Exception, partial_results: Optional[List[AgentResult]] = None ) -> str: """ Handle workflow failure with graceful degradation.
Full implementation in Story 3.7. Basic version for AC5. """ logger.error( "Workflow failed", extra={ "error_type": type(error).__name__, "error_message": str(error), "partial_results_count": len(partial_results) if partial_results else 0 } )
if partial_results: return f"Workflow partially completed. {len(partial_results)} agents succeeded." else: return "Workflow failed. Please try a simpler query."
module.testingNotes: - Unit test: Test timeout detection logic - Unit test: Test partial result handling - Integration test: Simulate agent failure, verify fallback behavior
